findings.chapter: Preface — The Architect's Evidence Discipline (p. xi)
findings.evidence: PDF p. 17: "ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example ([canonical scenario] or [ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED), on the book's teaching geometry, to be re-derived per deployment." | "Provenance (Axis 1) records where the number came from: ... [ILLUSTRATIVE] a non-canonical worked-example or scenario input chosen to make a calculation concrete, ..." | "The third axis — measurement status (ANALYTICAL / ILLUSTRATIVE / MODELED / MEASURED, or UNMEASURED where the stage is not yet determined) — rides with that pair or stands alone."
findings.issue: [ILLUSTRATIVE] is defined twice, on two different axes, with two different meanings. On Axis 1 (provenance) it means 'a non-canonical worked-example or scenario input chosen to make a calculation concrete'. On Axis 3 (measurement status) it means 'a chosen scenario input or worked example ... on the book's teaching geometry'. The Axis-3 definition explicitly includes the canonical scenario, which Axis 1 explicitly excludes from [ILLUSTRATIVE]. Every [ILLUSTRATIVE]-tagged cell in the book (Ch 3 Tables 3-2/3-3, Ch 5 Table 5-2, Ch 7 Figs 7.1/7.4/7.5/7.6/7.7/7.8) is therefore ambiguous: the reader cannot tell from the tag whether the number is canonical or non-canonical, or whether the tag is provenance or measurement status.
findings.fix_instruction: Rename one of the two. Keep [ILLUSTRATIVE] as the Axis-1 provenance tag (non-canonical worked example) and rename the Axis-3 measurement-status member to something distinct (e.g. MODELLED / SCENARIO-DERIVED), then add one line in the Preface's evidence-boundary panel stating which axis the surviving [ILLUSTRATIVE] belongs to. Apply the rename to the Axis-3 list only.
